title: Metabolism

result: Educational review. Insulin, released after eating, binds the insulin receptor, a tyrosine kinase that autophosphorylates and recruits insulin receptor substrate, leading to phosphorylation of AKT; in skeletal muscle, heart and adipose tissue insulin signalling translocates GLUT4 from internal vesicles to the plasma membrane; insulin inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase in adipose tissue; glucagon, released as blood glucose falls, acts mainly on the liver through a G-protein-coupled receptor that raises cAMP. Gluconeogenesis bypasses the irreversible steps of glycolysis with pyruvate carboxylase, activated by acetyl-CoA, phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase, fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase and glucose-6-phosphatase. Because pyruvate dehydrogenase is irreversible and the carbon entering the citric acid cycle as acetyl-CoA is lost in its decarboxylation steps, fats cannot produce glucose at a net rate; the glyoxylate cycle, which bypasses these steps in plants, bacteria, fungi, algae and protozoa, is stated not to exist in animals.
